blogs.title: Why Token-Level RL Breaks at Scale—and the Simple Fix
blogs.description: Large language models are rewarded for entire answers, yet many RL methods tweak probabilities one token at a time. This mismatch injects noisy, high-variance updates that pile up over long responses and can trigger model collapse. This post explains why aligning the unit of optimization with the unit of reward (the whole sequence) is the key insight behind GSPO.

blogs.title: GSPO in Plain English: Reward the Whole Answer, Not Each Word
blogs.description: GSPO measures how likely a full response is under the new policy versus the old one and optimizes at the sequence level. By clipping entire responses and using group-normalized rewards as advantages, it produces cleaner, more stable learning signals. Think of it as grading the essay, not each word in isolation.

blogs.title: Clipping, Reimagined: Cutting Whole Responses Yields Cleaner Gradients
blogs.description: Traditional methods clip token-by-token, but GSPO clips at the response level and still learns faster—even when it clips more aggressively. We unpack why fewer but cleaner gradients beat many noisy ones, and how length normalization keeps importance ratios well-behaved across answers of different lengths.

blogs.title: MoE Without Meltdowns: How GSPO Tames Expert Routing Volatility
blogs.description: Mixture-of-Experts models can reshuffle which experts activate after each update, destabilizing token-level corrections and derailing training. GSPO sidesteps this by focusing on sequence likelihoods, removing the need for complex workarounds like Routing Replay. The result: simpler, stabler MoE RL that uses the model’s full capacity.

blogs.title: Less Plumbing, More Learning: GSPO Simplifies RL Infrastructure
blogs.description: Token-level recomputation to match training and inference precisions can bloat RL pipelines. Because GSPO relies on sequence-level likelihoods, it’s more tolerant to precision differences and can often use inference-engine outputs directly. This streamlines partial rollouts, multi-turn RL, and disaggregated training–inference workflows.

blogs.title: From PPO to GRPO to GSPO: The Road to Stable RL for LLMs
blogs.description: PPO depends on a heavyweight value model; GRPO avoids it by using group-relative rewards—but keeps token-level updates that can get noisy. GSPO completes the evolution by moving importance weighting and clipping to the sequence level, aligning optimization with reward and improving stability and efficiency.

blogs.title: Fine-Grained When You Need It: GSPO-token for Multi-Turn Feedback
blogs.description: Sometimes you want per-token advantages—for example, in multi-turn interactions. GSPO-token lets you assign token-wise advantages while retaining GSPO’s sequence-level importance ratio and stability. When all token advantages are equal, it’s numerically identical to GSPO, offering flexibility without sacrificing robustness.

blogs.title: What It Delivers: Efficiency, Stability, and Qwen3’s Gains
blogs.description: GSPO trains stably over longer generations, scales with more compute, and converts samples into progress more efficiently than GRPO. In practice, it boosts performance on challenging math and coding benchmarks and has powered notable improvements in the latest Qwen3 models. We translate the empirical curves into real-world takeaways for practitioners.
